questions.q: Why does the critical path for Course Registration actually require two separate UI Tests rather than one?
options: Because the happy path cannot be tested with ATF at all
Because registering for an open section and hitting a full section exercise completely different logic, and both have to be proven
Because UI Tests can only ever check one field at a time
Because ServiceNow requires at least two UI Tests per Test Suite by default
questions.explain: A student registering for an open section and a student hitting a full section are distinct scenarios with distinct expected outcomes, so each gets its own explicit UI Test.

questions.q: In the full-section rejection UI Test, what specifically must the assertions confirm about the section's seat count?
options: Seat count is not something an ATF test can check
That the seat count is reset to zero after the rejection
That the seat count increased by one despite the rejection
That the seat count did not change at all, since a rejected registration must not quietly consume a seat
questions.explain: A rejected registration must leave the section's seat count untouched — confirming that is as important as confirming the student saw a rejection message.

questions.q: Why does the capacity-check logic also get its own server-side Test, even though the UI Tests already exercise it indirectly?
options: A server-side Test catches a bug in the capacity math directly, even if a future UI change made the broken logic merely look correct on screen
The UI Tests cannot call server-side logic under any circumstances
Server-side Tests are required before any UI Test can run
Server-side Tests replace the need for UI Tests entirely
questions.explain: Testing the logic directly, independent of the UI, protects against the UI accidentally masking a real defect in the underlying capacity math.

questions.q: What does the server-side capacity-check Test assert when given a section with max_seats = 30 and enrolled_count = 30?
options: That the capacity-check function returns true, meaning a seat is available
That the test cannot run because the section is full
That the capacity-check function returns false, meaning no seat is available
That the section record is deleted automatically
questions.explain: With enrolled_count equal to max_seats, there is no open seat, so the function must correctly return false.

questions.q: Why are all three tests grouped into one Test Suite scheduled to run on every pipeline build, rather than run manually before each release?
options: So a regression introduced at any point is caught immediately, long before it's anywhere near a Change Request
Because ATF Test Suites cannot be run manually under any circumstances
Because grouping tests into a suite makes each individual test run faster
Scheduling on every build is required by ServiceNow licensing, not for any testing reason
questions.explain: Running the suite on every build, triggered by every commit, catches regressions as they happen rather than discovering them right before a release.
